name: BSP_Localization_ParseTableFile
evidence: Hypothesis, not a recovered symbol. Takes the manager in ECX plus an 8-byte native string by value and two ints on the stack. Collects every mount holding the name (00bdef90) and parses each stream. Record grammar from the three states of local_4f80: ASCII token to a space, second ASCII token to a space, then 16-bit units until the unit pair 0x0A00,0x0D00 (file bytes 00 0A 00 0D). The key is token1 + "." (00ce3a70) + token2 in a 152-byte stack buffer; the text is UTF-16LE in a 19994-byte buffer; neither is bounds-checked. Values go into the map through 00a9fc30, so a repeated key overwrites. When the second int argument is zero it then reads the same name with "x" appended (00ceb488), a flat array of 16-bit pairs appended to the vectors at manager +0x4020 and +0x4030. Validated against the installed lockit/englishauthentic.lan: 6864 records, 6864 terminators, whole file consumed. Evidence: docs/APP_INIT_LOCALE.md; reports/app_init_locale.json.

name: BSP_Localization_ReloadTables

name: BSP_Localization_LoadTable

name: BSP_GuiManager_SetEnabled
evidence: Hypothesis, not a recovered symbol. Packet game_blocking_screen_frame, read-only analysis. Provisional. __thiscall, ECX = the 0x88-byte cGuiManager, one byte stack argument, RET 4. Stores the argument at manager+0x48 (a byte the constructor 00aa5d70 zeroes) and, only when it is zero, tail-JMPs to the virtual +0x34 of manager+0x50 with the argument slot rewritten to 0. manager+0x50 is MousePtrFE_Icon (docs/APP_INIT_FONTS_GUI.md resource 4) and +0x34 is the visibility setter, so a disable also hides the front-end mouse pointer. The decompiler's jumptable warning at 00aa0e1b is the tail JMP. Nine call sites; in BSP_Game_OnMove 004e4c4d passes 0 and 004e4c5c passes 1 on the two halves of the branch on byte DAT_00f8abe8+0x3e8.

name: BSP_GuiManager_SetPointerVisible
evidence: Hypothesis, not a recovered symbol. Packet game_blocking_screen_frame, read-only analysis. Provisional. Four instructions at 00aa0e50-00aa0e58: ECX = manager+0x50, then a bare JMP to that object's virtual +0x34 without pushing anything, so it forwards its own stack frame. All four call sites push one argument before fetching the manager (004e4c38 pushes 0, 00565081, 004daa9d and 004c6e1c likewise), which makes the real signature __thiscall f(cGuiManager*, bool) with the callee cleaning the argument; Ghidra's zero-argument __fastcall signature and its jumptable warning at 00aa0e58 are both artefacts of the tail JMP. manager+0x50 is MousePtrFE_Icon. Unlike BSP_GuiManager_SetEnabled it never touches manager+0x48.

name: BSP_GuiManager_Update
evidence: Hypothesis, not a recovered symbol. Packet game_on_move_map, read-only analysis. Provisional. Four callers; in BSP_Game_OnMove it is called only immediately after BSP_GuiManager_GetOrCreate (004e4b67 on the blocking-screen fast path, 004e4cb8 on the front-end path), with the raw frame delta and a zero second argument, and immediately before BSP_Game_Render. | Packet game_blocking_screen_frame: __thiscall, ECX = the 0x88-byte cGuiManager, stack arguments float seconds then a byte flag, RET 8; both BSP_Game_OnMove call sites pass flag 0. Body: byte manager+0x70 = flag; if flag == 0, 00aa3910(manager) runs the pointer hit-test pass over the cursor vector at DAT_00f8bbf4+0x94; BSP_GuiManager_ResetScreens (00aa0f70) hides hl_FrameBox at +0x74 and hlCircle_FrameBox at +0x78; 004d35d0 copy-constructs a temporary vector from the screen vector at manager+0x18/+0x1c so the walk is over a snapshot; each element is updated through its virtual +0x40(seconds) when its virtual +0x38 returns non-zero or BSP_GuiScreen_HasLiveEntries does; on exit manager+0x70 is cleared unconditionally and the snapshot is freed. The interleaved 00bf6713 calls are _SECURE_SCL assertions.

name: BSP_GuiManager_Construct
evidence: Hypothesis, not a recovered symbol. __fastcall f(void *this) returning this, RET, body 00aa5d70-00aa5e18, sole caller 004c12b0 BSP_GuiManager_GetOrCreate. Vtable 00d5bfcc. Stores a node from 00aa2920 at +0xc, sets its byte +0x15 to 1 and self-links its +0/+4/+8 pointers as a sentinel; zeroes +0x10 and +0x18..+0x30; stores 00aa2820's result at +0x38; zeroes +0x3c, +0x40, byte +0x48 and +0x6c; copies the float DAT_00ce3800 into +0x5c and +0x60. It leaves +0x4c, +0x50, +0x54, +0x58 and +0x74..+0x84 uninitialised, exactly the fields 00aa5e20 fills, which is the ordering evidence that the resource load must run once after construction. The segment-76 literal cGuiManager is the only direct name support. Evidence: docs/APP_INIT_FONTS_GUI.md; reports/app_init_fonts_gui.json.

name: BSP_GuiManager_LoadResources
evidence: Hypothesis, not a recovered symbol. __fastcall f(void *this), ECX = the 0x88-byte GUI manager, RET, body 00aa5e20-00aa633e. Sole caller 0073bae0 at 0073bc20. Loads a fixed ten-entry resource list: data/interface/textures/whiteGui.tga (00d5c084) into +0x28 behind a BSP_VFS_ResolveExistingName gate at 00aa5e88 and interface/textures/common/transparent.tga (00d5c058) into +0x2c, both through renderer *(00f8d394) virtual +0x64; then group _Mouse (00d5c050) via 00aa5840 into +0x4c, children MousePtrFE_Icon (00d5c040) into +0x54 and +0x50 and MousePtrGUI_Icon (00d5c02c) into +0x58 via 00aa7e00 with ECX = [+0x4c]; then group _Highlight (00d5c020) via 00aa5840 kept only in EDI, and children hl_FrameBox, hlCircle_FrameBox, safezone_43_FrameBox and safezone_169_FrameBox into +0x74, +0x78, +0x7c and +0x80 with ECX = that group. 00aa5840 always takes the manager, 00aa7e00 always takes a group. Each widget is followed by a virtual +0x34(bool); MousePtrFE_Icon's is deferred to 00aa60a3, after MousePtrGUI_Icon's. Byte +0x84 is cleared last at 00aa6305. Six blocks are reported unreachable by the decompiler, so the literals were read from the listing. Evidence: docs/APP_INIT_FONTS_GUI.md; reports/app_init_fonts_gui.json.

name: BSP_GuiScreen_HasLiveEntries
evidence: Hypothesis, not a recovered symbol. Packet game_blocking_screen_frame, read-only analysis. Provisional. __fastcall, ECX = a cGuiScreen, no arguments, returns AL. Scans the screen+0x8c dword-counted array of pointers at screen+0x88 and returns 1 at the first non-null element, 0 otherwise. Its only observed use is in BSP_GuiManager_Update at 00aa500c, as the fallback that makes a screen whose virtual +0x38 said no still receive its virtual +0x40 update, so the array holds work that must drain even while the screen is not being drawn.
